subject: Runbook ops warmup + POC working session scheduling
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Avery Systems <ops@averysystems.com>; Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@clearline.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Runbook ops warmup + POC working session scheduling

Hi Liam / Avery team,

Thanks again for agreeing to a hands-on POC. We want to run a short runbook/warmup + an interactive working session focused on:
- Prompt review and edge cases (safety & hallucination traps)
- Routing topology (latency vs cost lanes, fallback policies)
- Load validation: small-scale surge + steady-state throughput checks

Proposed slots (PT):
- Option A: Tue Aug 3, 10:00–11:30 PT
- Option B: Thu Aug 5, 10:00–11:30 PT

Agenda will be ~90 minutes: 15m runbook review, 45m hands-on routing/load, 20m action items + next steps. I attached the initial runbook and a starter load profile. Can you confirm the preferred slot and whether you need VPC access or sample data? Also please share a rough estimate of peak tokens per request so Ben can size the harness.

Attachments: redwood_runbook_v1.pdf (pdf), load_profile_q3.csv (csv)

Thanks — I’ll lock the calendar once we confirm.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
T: +1 415 555 0123
https://redwood.com
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@clearline.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runbook ops warmup + POC working session scheduling

Tessa,

Thanks — Thu Aug 5 at 10:00 PT works best for our ops and infra folks. We do not require VPC access for this initial warmup; a secure test tenant is fine.

A few quick notes so your team can size the load: average request is ~450 tokens in/out, peak concurrent user simulations we’d like to validate up to ~2k concurrent conversational sessions (burst to 6k for 10 minutes to test autoscale). We also make a helper embedding call for search on ~1 in 5 requests.

Can Ben confirm whether the harness will support the embedding call pattern (i.e., mixed text+embedding traffic)?

—Liam
Liam O'Neill
Head of Platform Integrations | Clearline (Avery Systems partner)
liam.oneill@clearline.com

Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runbook ops warmup + POC working session scheduling

Great — locking Thu Aug 5, 10:00–11:30 PT. I created a tentative calendar invite (meeting link: https://meet.redwood.com/meet/pocteam) and attached an updated runbook with a more detailed agenda.

Quick owners and pre-work so we come prepared:
- Ben Carter: build the load harness and include embedding-call simulation (ramp 0→2k conc. users; burst to 6k for 10m). Please provide the harness run command and expected infra footprint by EOD Mon Aug 2.
- Kimberly Park: finalize the prompt suite and corner-case examples. Please add 8–10 prompts to the shared Drive folder and flag anything that requires safety filters.
- Dev Patel: prepare a dedicated test environment (model pinned to ver-s3) and a small KV cache seed we can use during the session. Provide access instructions for the Redwood test tenant.

On the agenda itself: we will spend the first 15 minutes walking through the runbook, then hand control to Ben/Dev for the load sequences while Kimberly runs the prompt validation cases. We’ll keep a live action log in the Drive link below.

Action items summary (pre-session):
- Ben: harness + command + infra estimate (due 2026-08-02)
- Kimberly: prompt suite in Drive (due 2026-08-03)
- Dev: test env access + KV seed (due 2026-08-03)

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcExample
Runbook attached: redwood_runbook_v1.pdf

Thanks — appreciate the quick coordination.

Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runbook ops warmup + POC working session scheduling

Quick update from my side — I will have the harness ready and can simulate the mixed traffic pattern. Plan:
- Harness: containerized runner (docker image: redwood/load-harness:202607)
- Scenario: steady ramp to 2k concurrent over 15m, 10m burst to 6k, back down to 1k steady; embedding call on ~20% of requests
- Infra footprint estimate: 6 x A100 equiv GPUs for the burst window (we will test autoscale behavior against 3x baseline nodes)

Please confirm the max seq length we should test — Liam earlier noted ~450 tokens average; do you want us to include 1k-token worst-case for a small subset of tests?

Attachment: load_profile_q3.csv (contains ramp schedule and client weights)

On Thu, Jul 30, 2026 at 08:45 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com> wrote:

Thanks,
Ben
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@clearline.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runbook ops warmup + POC working session scheduling

All — confirming Aug 5, 10:00 PT. Appreciate the owners and the clarity. Final pre-session notes from our side:
- Max sequence length: include a couple of 1k-token tests (5% of traffic) to exercise KV cache and attention memory.
- Embedding calls: include with the 20% pattern; we’ll provide a small vector index (search corpus) by EOD Mon (Drive link).
- Success criteria for the session: no more than a 500ms p95 added latency for routing fallbacks, and graceful degradation during the 6k burst (no errors > 1%).

Post-session request: please add a 60–90 minute follow-up deep-dive where we review logs, traces, and cost telemetry. Prefer the week of Aug 9 — can we pencil Wed Aug 11 or Thu Aug 12?

Action recap (for calendar invite & drive action log):
- Ben: harness & infra estimate (due 2026-08-02)
- Kimberly: prompt suite + corner cases (due 2026-08-03)
- Dev: test env + KV seed + access (due 2026-08-03)
- Avery/Clearline: search corpus + validation data (due 2026-08-02)

Thanks — see you Thu.

—Liam
